title: Runtime schema negotiation layer for analytics SDK/CLI/API compatibility
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We will build a thin runtime schema negotiation layer that sits in front of the telemetry ingestion pipeline (gateway) and coordinates schema compatibility across SDKs, CLI, and public API clients. The goal is to allow safe, incremental schema evolution without breaking ingestion consumers or losing observability data.

Goals and success criteria:
- Allow SDK/CLI/API to publish a schema version header or client capability token and have the gateway translate/normalize to the canonical ingestion envelope.
- Maintain backwards compatibility for at least two historical schema generations by default.
- Reduce error rate for ingestion schema mismatches to <0.01% after rollout.
- Provide fast, actionable diagnostics in Console (per-client error rates, sample malformed events) and automatic fallback to shimmed normalization.

Approach overview:
1) Define a lightweight capability negotiation header (X-Redwood-Schema: vX or X-Redwood-Capabilities: json-array) that SDK/CLI will set. New SDK releases will set the latest version; older SDKs continue sending earlier versions.
2) Implement a negotiation service as an attachable module in the ingestion gateway. The service: (a) validates header, (b) looks up transformation pipeline (proto/JSON transforms) for incoming version -> canonical vN, (c) applies transforms, and (d) emits a normalized event envelope.
3) Store transformation rules in a versioned artifact store (git-backed + immutable release tags). The gateway will cache transformation rules and reload on change.
4) Provide an adapter shim for clients that cannot set headers (older CLI or third-party infra) by inferring schema from event shape and routing to best-match transform with lower confidence and higher sampling for alerts.

Tradeoffs and rationale:
- Why a runtime negotiator vs. hard-breaking version bumps: runtime negotiation allows gradual client upgrades, minimizes data loss, and defers expensive coordinated rollouts across customers. It adds complexity to the gateway and requires robust testing.
- Why not full universal schema: we retain a canonical ingestion envelope to simplify downstream analytics and retention policies; negotiation performs necessary normalization rather than proliferating variants downstream.
- Storage of transforms as artifacts (vs. DB drives): git-backed artifacts provide auditability and simple rollback semantics aligned with release processes.

Compatibility matrix and rollback plan:
- Supported client versions: current (v3), previous (v2), and legacy (v1, compatibility mode).
- Rollout stages: internal dev (gate disabled), canary (10% of traffic routed through negotiation), staged ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%), global enable with safety gates.
- Fallback: if a transform fails validation or runtime errors occur, gateway will route event to a quarantine stream and fall back to passthrough with an error tag to avoid blocking production traffic. Quarantine is subject to retention policy and triggers an alert.

Validation and testing:
- Unit tests for each transform (round-trip apply + backward-compat checks).
- Integration harness that replays representative telemetry bundles across schema versions (we will extend ENG-17789 validation harness).
- Canaries with synthetic traffic and a small cohort of internal customers. Monitor: malformed_count, transform_latency_p50/p95, ingestion_error_rate, per-client drop rate.

Observability and dashboards:
- New Console dashboard: "Schema Negotiation" showing per-client schema header distribution, transform errors, quarantine samples, and trend of normalized vs. passthrough events.
- Alerting: page on >=1% of events quarantined for >5 minutes or transform latency p95 > 400ms for >5 minutes.

Operational runbook highlights:
- How to roll back a transform: tag a previous transform artifact and trigger a cache invalidation endpoint.
- How to inspect a quarantined event and request a temporary bypass.
- Owner rotation: telemetry infra on-call for first 3 months, then shift to platform infra.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we standardize on header X-Redwood-Schema or a capabilities JSON header? (early preference: simple header for wide language SDK support)
- Retention policy for quarantined events (30 days vs. 90 days).
- Security review for transform artifact update flow (who can push transforms; require signed artifacts).

Artifacts and links:
- Implementation doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/telemetry/schema-negotiator (design + API examples)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingestion-gateway/pull/4123
- Validation harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-harness/tree/negotiator-prototype
- Draft Console dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/schema-negotiation (internal view)

Next steps (short-term):
- Finalize header format and update SDK/CLI team with spec (owner: Aisha).
- Merge prototype gateway module behind feature flag (owner: Liam).
- Add transform artifact signing and deploy canary.
- Run 2-week canary and evaluate metrics before widening rollout.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial write-up and spec posted. Asked SDK team for feedback on header format. Marking as P1 due to downstream analytics dependence.

2026-02-25 - Marina Ortiz (SDK): SDK team prefers a single header (X-Redwood-Schema: vX) for cross-language simplicity. We'll add optional capabilities header in a follow-up. SDK will ship v3 with header in next sprint.
2026-03-02 - Liam Chen: Prototype PR opened implementing negotiator module behind feature flag. Basic transform cache and artifact loader implemented. Unit tests added for v1->v3 transforms.
2026-03-04 - QA: Integration replay failed for a sampled v2 event with nested metadata arrays; transform produced an unexpected null in `request.user_id`. Added fix and additional unit tests.
2026-03-07 - Ops: Canary config ready. Routing rule will send 10% of traffic for team-internal API keys first. Alert hooks created for quarantine spikes.
2026-03-10 - Security review request: pending; raised question about artifact signing and RBAC for transform pushes. Security assigned to review (ETA 2026-03-16).
